Algebra 3/4 · Factoring

Difference of Perfect Squares & Higher Order Polynomials

One more factoring pattern, then a flowchart that puts every method together. Have your notebook open to pages 70–71.

x2 − 25  ⟶  (x − 5)(x + 5)

Page 70 · Factoring Difference of Perfect Squares

Use this method when you have two terms that:

• are both perfect squares

• are being subtracted

Page 70 · Pattern

(a2 − b2) =
(a − b)(a + b)
(a2 + b2)
prime: it can’t be factored

Page 70 · Example 1 · Factor the polynomials

x2 − 25

a = x, b = 5
(x − 5)(x + 5)

25x2 − 49

a = 5x, b = 7
(5x − 7)(5x + 7)

Page 70 · Example 2 · Factor the polynomials

4x6 − 9y2

a = 2x³, b = 3y
(2x³ − 3y)(2x³ + 3y)

2x4 − 8x2

2x²(x² − 4)
2x²(x − 2)(x + 2)

Page 71 · Factoring Higher Order Polynomials

For higher order polynomials, you are going to combine all of the skills we have been practicing from pages 56–70.

Is there a GCF?  Yes → factor out the GCF · No → keep going

Difference of Perfect Squaresa² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)
X-Methodax² ± bx ± ca · c on top, b on bottom
Factor by Groupingor Box Method
  • Once you complete a factoring method, start from the top again.
  • If it doesn't fit any of the patterns, check for a GCF. If it still doesn't, you're done!

Wrap-up

You've got it

  1. Two terms, both perfect squares, subtracted: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).
  2. A sum of squares, a² + b², is prime.
  3. GCF first. Then count the terms and pick a method.
  4. After every method, start from the top again. done
Optional

Practice on your own

Four problems. For each one:

  1. Work it in your notebook. GCF first!
  2. Stuck? Hint 1 gets you started. Hint 2 shows a and b.
  3. Pick your answer to check it. Wrong answers tell you what to fix.

Practice 1 of 4 Optional

Factor completely: x2 − 49

Hint 1 · Where to start

Two terms, both perfect squares, subtracted. What times itself is 49?

Hint 2 · The pieces

a = x, b = 7.

Solution
(x − 7)(x + 7)

Practice 2 of 4 Optional

Factor completely: 16x2 − 81

Hint 1 · Where to start

16x² = (4x)² and 81 = 9². Use the pattern.

Hint 2 · The pieces

a = 4x, b = 9.

Solution
(4x − 9)(4x + 9)

Practice 3 of 4 Optional

Factor completely: 3x2 − 75

Hint 1 · Where to start

3 and 75 aren't perfect squares. GCF first: 3(x² − 25).

Hint 2 · The pieces

a = x, b = 5, with the 3 out front.

Solution
3(x − 5)(x + 5)

Practice 4 of 4 Optional

Factor completely: x2 + 36

Hint 1 · Where to start

Look at the sign between the terms. Is it a difference?

Hint 2 · The pieces

It's a sum of squares, and there's no GCF.

Solution
Prime (it can’t be factored)
